issues.legal_issue: A master plan lawfully prepared after the commencement of the land-ceiling regime may be considered in determining whether land is vacant land for the purpose of assessing land held in excess of the ceiling limit.
material_facts: The High Court invalidated proceedings under the land-ceiling regime, relying on an earlier decision to hold that authorities could not treat land as vacant land through a master plan prepared after the regime commenced.
The appeals required the Court to decide whether the master plan in force at commencement alone governed the determination of vacant land.
issues.conclusion: A master plan prepared in accordance with the law, including one prepared after the regime commenced, must be considered when determining whether land is vacant land. The earlier decision was incorrect to the extent that it held otherwise.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 2(h), 2(o), and 2(q) define master plan, urban land, and vacant land; section 2(o)(C) provides that land specified in a master plan for a non-agricultural purpose is not deemed to be used mainly for agriculture. Section 6(1) and its explanation provide that, where land that was not vacant becomes vacant for any reason, the commencement date for that land is the date it becomes vacant. Read with sections 3, 4, and 6 to 16, these provisions contemplate that land may acquire the character of vacant land after the regime commences and that statements may be required when that occurs. Master plans are not static because planning and development continue to change. The Court held that Atia Mohammadi Begum v. State of U.P. was incorrect to the extent it barred consideration of a later master plan; its discussion in Her Highness Maharani Shantidevi P. Gaikwad v. Savjibhai Haribhai Patel that planning does not freeze at commencement was consistent with this conclusion.

predicates.urban_land_ceiling_proceeding: The proceeding determines whether land in an urban area is vacant land held in excess of a ceiling limit.
predicates.relevant_later_master_plan_exists: A master plan relevant to the land was prepared after the land-ceiling regime commenced and was prepared in accordance with the law then in force.
predicates.later_master_plan_considered_in_vacancy_: The later master plan is considered in deciding whether the land is vacant land.

issues.definition: When a ceiling proceeding concerns urban land and a relevant master plan was lawfully prepared after commencement, the plan is considered in deciding whether the land is vacant.
